clue.text: One embracing a decisive argument

definitions.meaning: one who clinches, in the boxing or lovers' sense of holding someone tight
the point that settles a debate once and for all

explanation.surface: Someone hugging another while also winning the debate.
explanation.definitionFit: To clinch is to grip in an embrace or to settle a matter conclusively, so the noun covers both a hugger and a knockdown point.

clue.text: It's likely, at the outside, two states are enthusiastic

indicators.note: the outside of the word likely means its first and last letters only

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
CAL is an abbreviation for California, a second US state

explanation.surface: Someone predicting that a couple of American states will be keen on something.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrical in the sense of gushing: waxing lyrical means praising with great eagerness.

clue.text: Book matches — they're a new departure

parts.note: a novel is a book of fiction
ties are sporting fixtures, matches between teams, as in cup ties

explanation.surface: A book of matches presented as an innovation.
explanation.definitionFit: Novelties are fresh, unusual things, each a break from what came before.

clue.text: Island-it is appropriate for one seeking seclusion

parts.note: Herm is one of the small Channel Islands
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small island suits someone who wants to be alone.
explanation.walkthrough: HERM is a small car-free Channel Island near Guernsey, fitting the surface's picture of a retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse who lives apart from society, traditionally for religious reasons, is the classic seeker of solitude.

clue.text: Bill for wood gone astray-one of his tricks?

definitions.text: Bill for wood gone astray-one of his tricks?

indicators.note: letters gone astray have wandered from their places, so these four words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An invoice for timber has gone missing, perhaps a prank by a mischievous sprite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' tells you to rearrange the letters of BILL FOR WOOD GONE, all fifteen of them. The whole clue is also the definition: a hobgoblin from English folklore known for pranks would be just the sort to make a bill go missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Puck, the mischievous fairy of English folklore and of Shakespeare's Dream, delights in tricks such as leading travellers astray.

clue.text: Soft, easily digested pickle

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft
light food is easy on the stomach

explanation.surface: A gentle, digestible relish to go with a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickle is a predicament or difficult situation, as is a sorry plight.

clue.text: An element, originally arsenic, can appear in fruit

indicators.note: these words say the pieces turn up inside the fruit

parts.note: a plum is a fruit

indicators.note: originally means the opening letter of arsenic

parts.note: a tin is a can for food

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: an element, starting with arsenic, shows up in fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appear in' puts A (the first letter of arsenic) plus TIN inside PLUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious metal, atomic number 78, is one of the chemical elements.

clue.text: Rising European, immersed in work, making a bomb

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the whole construction is read from the bottom up
one piece is plunged inside the other

parts.note: an erg is a unit of work in physics
a Dane, from Denmark, is a European

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming European, busy at work, building a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'immersed in' puts DANE inside ERG after its E, giving EDANERG; 'Rising' then turns that upwards to read the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-thrown explosive device is a small bomb.

clue.text: Walk about certainly of value

indicators.note: about means one word is wrapped around the other

parts.note: to tread is to walk
sure, as in a confident yes, means certainly

explanation.surface: Walking around something certainly worth having.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treasured is prized and held dear, so it is precious to its owner.

clue.text: Doctor has done with cattle-dealer

parts.note: over means finished or done

explanation.surface: A doctor has finished dealing with a livestock merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: A herder who drove livestock to market, often trading them there.

clue.text: Look after gloomy mouse

indicators.note: after says the word for look comes behind the gloomy word

parts.note: black means dark and gloomy, as in a black mood
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: Caring for a mouse that seems depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as 'care for', but split it: EYE goes after BLACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouse is slang for a bruise round the eye, the swollen purple shiner from a punch.

clue.text: Row, with no one backing a lowly worker

parts.note: to scull is to row with oars

indicators.note: backing means the two little words are read in the other direction

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An argument with nobody supporting a junior employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns NO plus I round to ION. 'Row' looks like a quarrel but means propelling a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen servant who did the menial washing-up was the humblest of household staff.

clue.text: At home with Prime Minister's family

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in
Bonar Law was a British Prime Minister in the 1920s; with the possessive this gives his name plus S

explanation.surface: Relaxing at home with the PM's relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Bonar Law was briefly British Prime Minister in 1922 to 1923; crosswords often use him for LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Relatives by marriage form part of one's wider family.

clue.text: Martyred saint has been buried

parts.note: lain is what someone has done who has lain in the earth, buried

explanation.surface: A martyred saint who now lies in a grave.
explanation.definitionFit: A martyr is put to death for their faith, so killed fits.

clue.text: Making up catches, I'm following a plan

indicators.note: making up means composing something new out of these letters

explanation.surface: Someone inventing excuses while sticking to a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making up' says rearrange CATCHES plus IM.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram-like drawing set out according to a scheme or outline is laid out to a design.

clue.text: Lout never disposed to offer his services. .

indicators.note: disposed means set out or arranged, so these letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A yob who never wants to help anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' says rearrange LOUT NEVER. The trailing dots lead into the next clue's surface but take no part in this wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To come forward freely and offer to do a job without being asked is what an unpaid helper does.

clue.text: During race, mistake is one to inspire dread

indicators.note: during means the following pieces sit within the race

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
an error is a mistake
taken as written

explanation.surface: A slip in the middle of a race causes fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During' puts ERROR plus IS inside TT, the Isle of Man motorcycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone using violence to frighten people for political ends literally spreads terror.

clue.text: Change of heart with number 22

indicators.note: a change of these letters means a rearrangement of them

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: Feeling differently about the twenty-second item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of' rearranges HEART into THREA. The definition is the answer to clue 22, used as a verb: to loom.
explanation.definitionFit: Clue 22's answer as a verb means to pose a danger, the same as warn of harm.

clue.text: … he is forced into the army, and fell

indicators.note: into says the anagram is put inside the army word

parts.note: a horde is a great army or throng

indicators.note: forced means the letters are pushed out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man conscripted, then killed in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' rearranges HE IS to SEHI; 'into' puts it inside HORDE. 'fell' looks like a verb, but it means an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Fell is an old word for an animal's skin or pelt, like the leather from a horse.

clue.text: Chap given money for listening to a poem

parts.note: Ron is a man's name, so a chap

indicators.note: for listening says the money word is heard rather than read

parts.note: dough is slang for money

explanation.surface: A man paid to hear a piece of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for listening' says DOUGH (slang for money) is taken by sound, giving the written DEAU.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a short French verse form with a refrain and only two rhymes.

clue.text: Press-gang

definitions.meaning: a throng that pushes and squeezes together
a group or set of people

explanation.definitionFit: A mass of people is a press or throng, and a group of friends is a gang or set.

clue.text: Crushed fabric

definitions.meaning: cloth made from tightly twisted wool yarn

explanation.surface: A creased piece of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To worst someone is to beat them soundly, and a smooth wool cloth carries the same name.

clue.text: Girl who distributed medals

indicators.note: distributed means the letters are handed out into a different order

explanation.surface: A young woman handing out awards.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for a young unmarried woman, as in a maiden in distress.

clue.text: Loom — people need one

parts.note: men means people in a general sense
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A weaving machine: every worker needs one.
explanation.definitionFit: To loom is to hang over menacingly, posing a threat.

clue.text: Delights in opponents' intrigues

parts.note: E and N, East and North, are opposing seats at the bridge table
amours are love affairs, secret intrigues

explanation.surface: Someone takes pleasure in their rivals' plotting.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South play East-West, so East and North sit as opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone into love is to captivate and please them.

clue.text: Two pegs given to man averse to drinking

parts.note: a tee is the golfer's peg the ball sits on
a tot is a small drink, and a peg is also a measure of spirits
Al is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man who doesn't drink is handed two pegs.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase gives two different pegs: the golfing tee and the drink, a peg of whisky being a tot.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who never takes alcohol abstains entirely from drink.

clue.text: It's tricky to move your head

parts.note: to shift is to move

indicators.note: the head of the word your is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Moving your head is awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shifty is evasive and untrustworthy, like a crafty dealer.

clue.text: A relation puts us. .

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'A relation puts us. .', ends with the dots: the rest of its wordplay, 'in the money' (US inside COIN), is printed as the opening of 27-across, so no money word is in this clue.

clue.text: … in the money — we will quarrel

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or row

explanation.surface: Rich people are sure to fall out.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots continue the previous clue's sentence; this clue stands on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy people are comfortably off, rolling in cash.
